value.evidence: Draft A is overly vague ('exploring options,' 'would like to hear experiences') and reads as a generic recap of the brief rather than a genuine community question. It omits concrete friction points (login/cost/performance concerns from F3, app size concerns from F4) that would resonate with the audience and invite targeted responses. Draft B preserves all six facts and articulates specific trade-offs the developer actually faces: setup complexity vs. local deployment, user friction vs. app bloat, and content control methods. It names the APIs under consideration (F2) and frames distinct sub-questions (fine-tuning necessity, content filtering feasibility) that community members can address with concrete advice. Both cite the same facts accurately, but B's specificity—naming OpenAI/Claude/Gemini, mentioning login/cost/performance explicitly, asking about fine-tuning and filtering—creates actionable community fit. A's restraint becomes evasiveness; B's detail becomes clarity without inventing unsupported claims. Neither violates forbidden claims or essential limitations.
